svg.title: HATARA Figure 2. Where one side's measure changes the other's risk, phone view
svg.desc: HATARA Figure 2: IX-01 A recovery path is also an attack path (antagonism, safety → security): The envelope's availability was bought with a route around its authenticity. Authenticate the recovery or remove it. Status: CSR-C-05 not implemented. IX-02 Test modes become a back door (antagonism, safety → security): Validation aids must be absent from reference builds, not merely unused. Status: CSR-C-07 partial. IX-03 A rejected frame is a lost function (antagonism, security → safety): A security rejection must end in the safety reaction: an announced take-over request, never a silent stop. Status: CSR-C-09 not implemented. IX-04 One lock serves both (mutual reinforcement, both): The reference lock closes a hazard and a threat with one mechanism. Verify it once, for both. Status: CSR-C-01 implemented, not verified. IX-05 A rejected image must leave the stock car (antagonism, security → safety): The item may stop, but the stock path must stay: the switches fall back to pass-through only while the pull-down holds (LS-33). Status: CSR-C-03 not implemented. IX-06 A fault reaction is a DoS lever (antagonism, safety → security): It stays safe only while the alert path survives the same attack; otherwise it is the silent loss of H-02 and H-06. Status: Alert path under the same attack not analysed. IX-07 The service mode trusts the ignition line (antagonism, safety → security): The lock needs an ignition signal the harness cannot fake. Until then it is a known gap. Status: Known gap (LS-28). IX-08 One counter serves both (mutual reinforcement, both): One counter and CRC closes a stuck-frame fault and an injected frame. Specify it once, for both. Status: CSR-C-09 not implemented. IX-09 The driver camera is also a privacy asset (antagonism, safety → security): Every frame the safety function keeps is a privacy exposure. Keep and upload only what it needs (CSG-08). Status: CSR-C-14 not confirmed. IX-10 Firmware integrity holds up SG-01…SG-07 (conditional dependency, security → safety): Until both are met, SG-01 to SG-07 do not hold against an attacker on the SoC. SG-08 needs CSG-03 instead (IX-11). Status: Recorded in WP-C-10 §8. IX-11 Screen and DM attacks reach H-07, H-09 (conditional dependency, security → safety): Found by this analysis, closed in WP-C-09 v0.8. The derived status reopens it if a link is dropped. Status: Closed: WP-C-09 §3 links them now. IX-12 An attacker picks the moment (antagonism, security → safety): For an attacker-triggered event E does not apply: the TARA's safety impact governs. No rating changes (DQ-420 A). Status: Recorded in WP-C-03 §2 (DQ-420 A).
svg.text: HATARA · where one side's measure changes the other's risk
One card per interaction of hatara_model.py: the safety side, the security side, the arrow from cause to
effect, what follows, and what ties it to the analyses.
WP-C-03 · WP-C-09 · WP-C-10 · Kriaa et al. types · phone view

g.title: IX-01: A recovery path is also an attack path
g.text: A recovery path is also an attack path
If the panda fails to boot, pandad flashes the development bootstub to bring it back
The same path flashes unauthenticated firmware onto the safety MCU (TS-03, risk 5)
The envelope's availability was bought with a route around its authenticity. Authenticate the recovery or remove it.

g.title: IX-02: Test modes become a back door
g.text: Test modes become a back door
Debug, maneuver and joystick modes exist to validate control on the bench and the road
They replace the control processes, so a local attacker gets actuation through them (TS-04)
Validation aids must be absent from reference builds, not merely unused.

g.title: IX-03: A rejected frame is a lost function
g.text: A rejected frame is a lost function
If the item stops controlling without telling the driver, that is silent loss (H-02, H-06)
Counter and CRC checks on received frames will reject forged and damaged frames
A security rejection must end in the safety reaction: an announced take-over request, never a silent stop.

g.title: IX-04: One lock serves both
g.text: The envelope must run the Toyota safety mode with its limits (SG-01 to SG-07)
No SoC command may change the safety mode or parameter (CSG-01, TS-02)
The reference lock closes a hazard and a threat with one mechanism. Verify it once, for both.

g.title: IX-05: A rejected image must leave the stock car
g.text: A rejected image must leave the stock car
Stock PCS must keep working whatever the item does (SG-07, H-08)
Verified boot leaves the panda unable to run firmware that fails its check
The item may stop, but the stock path must stay: the switches fall back to pass-through only while the pull-down holds

g.title: IX-06: A fault reaction is a DoS lever
g.text: A fault reaction is a DoS lever
Heartbeat loss or a controls mismatch withdraws authority at once, with an alert (LS-24)
An attacker who stalls SoC processes (TS-12) can trigger that withdrawal at will
It stays safe only while the alert path survives the same attack; otherwise it is the silent loss of H-02 and H-06.
Alert path under the same attack not analysed

g.title: IX-07: The service mode trusts the ignition line
g.text: The service mode trusts the ignition line
Diagnostics over the OBD port are allowed only with the ignition off, for service
An open ignition branch reads as ignition off while driving and releases that lock (LS-28)
The lock needs an ignition signal the harness cannot fake. Until then it is a known gap.

g.title: IX-08: One counter serves both
g.text: The brake frame has no counter or checksum, so a stuck value passes (LS-21)
CAN integrity adds a counter and CRC against injected frames (GAP-01)
One counter and CRC closes a stuck-frame fault and an injected frame. Specify it once, for both.

g.title: IX-09: The driver camera is also a privacy asset
g.text: The driver camera is also a privacy asset
Driver monitoring needs a cabin camera to catch inattention (H-09)
Its video is personal data that an attacker or a thief can take (TS-11, DS-08)
Every frame the safety function keeps is a privacy exposure. Keep and upload only what it needs (CSG-08).

g.title: IX-10: Firmware integrity holds up SG-01…SG-07
g.text: SG-01 to SG-07 rest on the envelope firmware; SG-08 rests on DM on the SoC (WP-C-04)
Safety-mode integrity (CSG-01) and firmware authenticity (CSG-02) protect that firmware
Until both are met, SG-01 to SG-07 do not hold against an attacker on the SoC. SG-08 needs CSG-03 instead (IX-11).

g.title: IX-11: Screen and DM attacks reach H-07, H-09
g.text: Screen and DM attacks reach H-07, H-09
WP-C-03 names spoofed HMI state for mode confusion (H-07); missed inattention is H-09
TS-04 can alter DM behaviour; WP-C-09 v0.8 adds DS-13 and DS-14 so it reaches H-07 and H-09
Found by this analysis, closed in WP-C-09 v0.8. The derived status reopens it if a link is dropped.

g.title: IX-12: An attacker picks the moment
g.text: The HARA's exposure E assumes a random fault, striking a situation as often as it occurs
An attacker on the SoC waits for the worst situation; the TARA rates safety impact without E
For an attacker-triggered event E does not apply: the TARA's safety impact governs. No rating changes (DQ-420 A).

svg.text: Types after Kriaa et al. (conditional dependency, mutual reinforcement, antagonism; independent pairs are not listed).
Requirement statuses from WP-C-10 §7; gap status from WP-C-09 §3. Generated by hatara_figures.py.
